summary:
- Focus: Sustainability statements in UniCredit’s 2024 Annual Report outlining sector-specific policies, commitments, governance, and product guidelines to manage environmental, social, and reputational risks across the Group.
- Mining sector policy: Applies to owners, operators, subsidiaries, subcontractors, and key suppliers across the full mine lifecycle (prospecting to post-closure). Aims to assess and mitigate environmental and social impacts and reputational risks through a structured Reputational and ESG Risk Assessment.
- Oil & Gas sector policy: Covers upstream and midstream activities and related contractors/suppliers. Establishes criteria and processes for Reputational and ESG Risk Assessment, acknowledges climate and unconventional/Arctic risks, and commits to supporting the sector’s energy transition while mitigating environmental, social, and reputational risks.
- Tobacco sector commitment: Group-wide exit from manufacturers/producers by end-2025, with relationships phased out from 2026. Since 2022: no new customers and no tobacco-related project finance. Signed the Tobacco Free Finance Pledge, aligning with SDG 3 and SDG 17. Commitment approved by the CEO and monitored under the Group Reputational Risk Management Global Policy.
- Water infrastructure (large dams) policy: Applies to owners/operators and financing across design, construction, operation, maintenance, upgrades, and decommissioning of large dams and related infrastructure (e.g., hydropower). Addresses biodiversity, environmental, and community impacts, recognizing large dams’ role in Net-Zero and energy transition.
- Natural capital and biodiversity statement: First comprehensive framework linking biodiversity and climate. Commits to sustainable financing, reducing operational impacts, avoiding activities in protected areas, and combating deforestation. Based on Equator Principles, IFC Performance Standards, World Bank EHS Guidelines, and the Finance for Biodiversity Pledge; published on UniCredit’s website.
- ESG product guidelines: Group-wide methodology (since end-2022) for ESG product classification and reporting to prevent greenwashing/social washing. Covers lending, bonds, investments, hedging, capital markets, transactional, and insurance products. Anchored to EU Taxonomy, ICMA principles, ISDA SLB/SLD guidance, LMA principles, EU Transition Finance recommendations, SFDR, MiFID II, and ESMA fund naming guidance. Local entities must implement verification processes; approved by the Group Non-Financial Risks and Controls Committee.
- Governance and oversight: Sensitive sector policies and ESG product guidelines approved by the Group Non-Financial Risks and Controls Committee; applied across UniCredit S.p.A. and Group entities under the Operational Risk Oversight model. Policy summaries available on the corporate website.
text:
Statement of natural capital and biodiversity : 
The statement illustrates UniCredit’s commitment towards natural capital and biodiversity preservation. It represents our first comprehensive Natural 
Capital framework in which biodiversity and climate issues are interrelated: we are committed to protecting natural capital by delivering sustainable 
financing solutions to clients and reducing the environmental impacts of our direct operations. Avoid operations in areas pro tected for biodiversity 
conservation purpose  as well as combat deforestation and forest degradation are fundamental principles for the Group.  
 
The Statement has been developed considering the point of view of stakeholders such as regulators, investors, civil society, NGOs, and it is based 
on the following internationally recognized standards and initiatives:  
• Equator Principles ; 
• International Finance Corporation (IFC) Performance Standards on Environmental and Social Sustainability ; 
• World Bank Group Environmental,  Health and Safety (EHS) Guidelines ; 
• Finance for Biodiversity Pledge (FfBP).  
 
The document represents a positioning paper on the topics of natural capital and biodiversity, and it is published on our ins titutional website.

title: ESG product guidelines:
heading: ESG p roduct guidelines :
start_phrase: The ESG product guidelines, applicable since end 2022, aim at establishing a consistent and comprehensive methodology for the classification and reporting of UniCredit’s ESG offering and at preventing the related risks of green washing and social washing.
summary:
- Overview of UniCredit’s sector-specific sustainability policies and commitments within the Consolidated Report on Operations – Sustainability statements, detailing governance, scope, and risk controls across sensitive industries.
- Mining sector regulation: Applies to owners/operators and key suppliers across the full mining lifecycle (prospecting to post-closure) and a wide range of minerals; focuses on assessing and mitigating environmental, social, and reputational risks; governed by the Group Non-Financial Risks and Controls Committee and applied across Group entities.
- Oil & Gas sector regulation: Standards for upstream and midstream activities and related contractors; sets criteria and processes for Reputational and ESG Risk Assessments; aims to limit environmental, social, and reputational risks while supporting sector energy transition; same Group governance and scope.
- Tobacco sector commitment: Public commitment to fully exit financing/manufacturing exposure by end-2025 and phase out all relationships with manufacturers/producers from 2026; no new clients or project finance since 2022 phase-in; signatory to the Tobacco Free Finance Pledge; applies Group-wide, approved by CEO, monitored via Reputational Risk Management policy.
- Water infrastructure (large dams) policy: Risk standards for owners/operators and financing of large dams and related hydropower assets across build, maintenance, upgrade, and decommissioning; recognizes biodiversity, community, and climate impacts and role in net-zero and energy transition; governed by the same Group committee.
- Statement on natural capital and biodiversity: First comprehensive framework linking climate and biodiversity; commits to sustainable financing, reducing operational impacts, avoiding activities in protected areas, and combating deforestation; references Equator Principles, IFC PS, World Bank EHS, Finance for Biodiversity Pledge; published as a positioning paper.
- ESG product guidelines: Group-wide methodology for ESG product classification and reporting to prevent greenwashing/social washing; aligned with EU Taxonomy, ICMA, ISDA, LMA, EU Transition Finance guidance, SFDR, MiFID II, and ESMA fund naming guidance; requires local implementation and verification processes; central ESG function supports structuring and conducts ex-post checks; internal policy with public abstract.
- Human rights commitment: Group-wide adherence to international standards (UDHR, ICCPR, ICESCR, ILO, UNGPs, OECD, UNGC, PRI, IFC PS, WB EHS, UNEP FI PRB, EPs, WEPs, UNDRIP); promotes equal opportunities, decent work, social dialogue, fair wages, and training; approved June 2024 by Group Non-Financial Risk Committee; monitored via existing Group policies (reputational risk, whistleblowing, anti-harassment); communicated internally and to stakeholders for feedback.
- Diversity, equity and inclusion global policy: Establishes principles to foster inclusive culture, prevent discrimination, and enhance employee well-being and performance; aligned with applicable laws; applies to all entities and employees with defined responsibilities and consequence management for third-party misalignment.

title: Human rights commitment:
heading: Human rights commitment :
start_phrase: The human rights commitment outlines UniCredit's dedication to upholding human rights across its key stakeholder groups, including employees, customers, suppliers, and communities.
summary:
- Overview of UniCredit’s sustainability governance within the 2024 Annual Reports and Accounts, focusing on ESG policies and commitments.

  - Scope: applies Group-wide across employees, customers, suppliers, and communities; local entities may develop and share best practices.

text:
The objective of the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Global Policy is to set out the principles by which UniCredit enhances i nclusion throughout the 
whole organisation, aiming to ensure that our policies, procedures, and behaviours promote diversity, equity and inclusion and create an 
environment where individual differences are valued.  
 
The diversity, equity and inclusion global policy positively impacts UniCredit by fostering equal opportunities, securing employment, and enhancing 
employee well -being through dedicated benefits and a healthy work environment. The policy also ensures respect for diversity, advancing an 
inclusive cor porate climate through initiatives that actively prevent discrimination. Key opportunities include becoming an employer of ch oice by 
cultivating a flexible, inclusive culture and improving employee performance th rough forward -looking training programmes.

all legal entities and to all employees of the Group. All UniCredit employees play an active role and ar e responsible for its application while specific 
functions play key roles in the process, as outlined.  
Although the Group cannot control the conduct of Third Parties, it does not condone behaviours not aligned with the principle s of this Policy and will 
adopt any appropriate consequence management.

Human rights commitment : 
The human rights commitment outlines UniCredit's dedication to upholding human rights across its key stakeholder groups, including employees, 
customers, suppliers, and communities. This document summarizes the roles and responsibilities as well as the principles, rul es, pro cedures and 
systems adopted by UniCredit to comply with generally accepted international and local standards and regulations for preventi ng, managing and, 
where possible, reducing human rights impacts.  
Grounded in international standards and conventions, this commitment contributes to equal opportunities, secure and quality e mployment, and the 
promotion of adequate wages, supported by social dialogue and collective bargaining. It also enhances employee w ell-being through dedicated 
activities and fosters skill development through training and professional growth programmes. Opportunities include positioni ng UniCredit as an 
employer of choice, improving employee performance with forward -thinking training, a nd ensuring transparent performance reviews and career 
development plans.  
 
UniCredit’s human rights commitment leverages on and respects:  
• the Universal Declaration of Human Rights ; 
• the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights ; 
• the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights ; 
• the International Labour Organization's (ILO) Fundamental Human Rights conventions (29, 87, 98, 100, 105, 111, 138 and 182) ; 
• the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights ; 
• the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises ; 
• the UN Global Compact principles ; 
• the UN Principles for Responsible Investment ; 
• the International Finance Corporation (IFC) Performance Standards ; 
• the World Bank Group Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) Guidelines ; 
• the United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) Principles for Responsible Banking ; 
• the Equator Principles (EP) ; 
• the Women's Empowerment Principles ; 
• the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples ; 
• the Declaration on Human Rights Defenders.  
 
The Commitment applies to all UniCredit group, while sole legal entities may develop local specific human rights best practices which can be 
disseminated across our Group, with a view to promoting continuous improvement.  
The current version of the Human Rights Commitment was approved by the Group Non Financial Risk Committee chaired by the Grou p CEO in 
June 2024. The monitoring of the effectiveness of the human rights commitment leverages on existing processes detailed in other Group's policies 
and managed by the related functions (for example, the Group Reputational Risk Management Global Policy, the Whistleblowing G lobal Policy, the 
Global Policy against harassment, se xual misconduct, bullying and retaliation).  
The Commitment is communicated to all employees through various internal initiatives that include, among others, internal com munication and news 
on local intranets. The Commitment is also published on the Group website. In addition, the relevant internal a nd external stakeholders will be 
informed about the Human Rights Commitment to collect their feedback and thus consider their expectations in reviewing our im provement plan.

title: Group remuneration policy:
heading: Group remuneration policy :
start_phrase: The Group remuneration p olicy defines the principles and standards which UniCredit applies in designing, implementing and monitoring the Group compensation practices, plans and systems.
summary:
- Overview: Extract from UniCredit’s 2024 Annual Reports and Accounts (Sustainability Statements) detailing groupwide policies and frameworks that govern ESG, human rights, DEI, remuneration, People & Culture, recruiting, and training.

- ESG deal governance: A central ESG function supports legal entities in structuring sustainable finance transactions (social/green/transition/ESG-linked) and performs periodic ex-post checks. The policy is for internal use with a public abstract online.

- Human Rights Commitment:
  - Scope: Applies across employees, customers, suppliers, and communities; groupwide with room for local best practices.
  - Content: Roles/responsibilities and systems to prevent, manage and reduce human rights impacts; promotes equal opportunities, quality and secure employment, adequate wages, social dialogue/collective bargaining, employee well-being, skills development, training, and transparent performance and career processes.
  - Standards referenced: UDHR, ICCPR, ICESCR, ILO core conventions, UNGPs, OECD Guidelines, UN Global Compact, UN PRI, IFC Performance Standards, World Bank EHS Guidelines, UNEP FI PRB, Equator Principles, Women’s Empowerment Principles, UNDRIP, and the Declaration on Human Rights Defenders.
  - Governance: Approved by the Group Non-Financial Risk Committee chaired by the Group CEO (June 2024). Effectiveness monitored via existing group policies (e.g., reputational risk, whistleblowing, anti-harassment).
  - Communication: Shared internally (intranets, communications) and published on the Group website; stakeholders are engaged for feedback to inform improvements.

- Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) Global Policy:
  - Aim: Embed inclusion throughout the organization; ensure policies, procedures, and behaviors promote DEI and prevent discrimination.
  - Benefits: Equal opportunities, secure employment, enhanced well-being, inclusive culture, forward-looking training; supports positioning as an employer of choice.
  - Scope and accountability: Applies to all entities and employees; aligned with applicable laws; sets expectations for third parties and enables consequence management for misalignment.
  - Transparency: Progress reported via Sustainability Statements and an annual DEI report (internal and external).

- Group Remuneration Policy:
  - Purpose: Principles and standards for compensation aligned with long-term strategy and sustainability; links pay to risk-adjusted performance; discourages excessive and sustainability-related risk-taking.
  - Impact: Supports equal opportunity, quality employment, fair compensation; promotes diversity, inclusion, and flexible work-life solutions.
  - Applicability: Across the organization, including external distribution networks; fully applied to Material Risk Takers with local adaptations.
  - Governance: Proposed by the Remuneration Committee, defined by the Board, and submitted annually to the AGM for approval.

- People & Culture Policy Framework:
  - Function: Central reference for HR/People & Culture global rules, plans, programs, and processes across UniCredit S.p.A., group legal entities, and foreign branches; update forthcoming.
  - Objectives: Consistent groupwide HR management; ensure employees have the skills and competencies needed; ensure regulatory compliance and foster professionalism and accountability.

- Recruiting Process Regulation:
  - Aim: Structured, transparent, and consistent recruitment/selection; compliance with labor and regulatory requirements; alignment with corporate values and Code of Conduct.
  - Principles: Fair, unbiased processes ensuring equal opportunities based on skills and qualifications.
  - Implementation: Internal regulation executed by Group People & Culture and line managers. References include CONSOB and Banca d’Italia regulations.

- Training and Education Guidelines:
  - Role: Central reference for People & Culture rules, programs, and processes at UniCredit S.p.A., to be extended groupwide.
  - Alignment: Meets Banca d’Italia Circular 285 requirements; ensures consistent management and that personnel have skills necessary for their responsibilities.
  - Access and governance: Published on the intranet; relevant actors engaged in review and validation.
text:
Group remuneration policy : 
The Group remuneration p olicy defines the principles and standards which UniCredit applies in designing, implementing and monitoring the Group 
compensation practices, plans and systems. The policy aligns with UniCredit's long -term strategy and commitment to sustainability by ensuring 
compensation is linked to risk -adjusted performance and discourages excessive risk -taking, including in the context of sustainability risks. This policy 
positivel y impacts the promotion of equal opportunities, quality employment, and fair compensation , further reinforced through social dialogue and 
collective bargaining. Opportunities arising from this policy include strengthening UniCredit’s position as an employer of ch oice, promoting diversity, 
fostering an inclusive culture, and offering flexible w ork-life balance solutions that meet evolving employee needs.  
 
The principles of the Group remuneration policy are valid across the entire organisation and shall be reflected in the remuneration practices applying 
to employee categories across businesses, including staff belonging to external distribution networks, considering their remu neration peculiarities . In 
compliance with the Group remuneration policy and local regulation, legal entities, countries, and divisions apply the compensation framework for all 
employees. Furthermore, the elements of the policy are full y applied across the entire Material Risk Taker population, with local adaptations based 
on specific regulations and/or business specifics, consistent with the overall Group approach.  
 
On an annual basis, the Group remuneration policy, as proposed by the Remuneration Committee, is defined by the Board of Directors, and then 
presented to the shareholders’ Annual General Meeting for approval, in line with regulatory requirements.

Recruiting process : 
The recruiting p rocess regulation aims to establish a structured framework for UniCredit group’s recruitment and selection processes, promoting 
transparency and consistency across all hiring practices. It ensures compliance with relevant labour laws and regulations16 while aligning with the 
Company’s core values and Code of Conduct. By fostering a fair and unbiased recruitment process, the regulation guarantees th at all candidates 
are treated with respect and given equal opportunity based on their skills and qualificat ions, thereby upholding the integrity and ethical standards of 
UniCredit group.  
 
The recruiting p rocess regulation is intended for internal use, and Group People & Culture functions and line managers are responsible for its 
implementation.

text:
The policy, aligned with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Group's values, outlines UniCredit’s commitment to fost ering a respectful 
and professional workplace free from harassment, sexual misconduct, bullying, and retaliation. The aim of this policy is the prevention, detection,

start_phrase: UniCredit statement demonstrates its commitment on promoting the respect for human rights, and it must be read in conjunction with human rights commitment.
summary:

title: Code of conduct:
heading: Code of conduct :
start_phrase: The code of conduct is available on our website.

- Global policy against harassment, sexual misconduct, bullying and retaliation: Aligns with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and Group values; aims at prevention, detection, enforcement, and monitoring; protects reporters (employees and third parties) from retaliation; applies to internal and external behaviors across all entities; promotes diversity, inclusion, and a respectful workplace.

- Modern Slavery Act and human trafficking statement: Annual disclosure since 2016 covering commitments to international norms (UK MSA 2015, ILO core conventions, UN Covenants, UNGPs, UNEP FI PRB); describes internal controls, supplier due diligence and minimum requirements, and employee training to mitigate slavery/trafficking risks; most recent statement approved by the Board and signed by the CEO in June 2024 (applicable to UniCredit S.p.A. and UniCredit Bank AG).

- Group privacy policy: Establishes a uniform Group framework for protecting personal data of individuals (employees, clients, and related persons) in line with GDPR and local laws; defines Data Controller accountability supported by the DPO; focuses on advisory, monitoring, and education to ensure trust and compliance.

- Customer Protection rules: Sets principles/standards for offering banking products and services across all channels and customer segments; maps to EU regulations (Consumer Credit, Mortgage Credit, Payment Accounts, PSD2 transparency, Deposit Guarantee, EBA POG guidelines); approved by the Group Compliance Officer; implementation monitored via internal tools.

- Code of conduct: Publicly available; mandates high professional conduct for employees and third-party partners; covers key compliance risks (client interest protection, antitrust, market integrity, AML/CTF, sanctions, anti-bribery/corruption, data protection); approved and overseen by the Board and top management; references additional country-specific ethics frameworks (e.g., Italy’s Decree 231/2001).

- Group tax strategy policy: Commits to full compliance with domestic/international tax laws, paying due taxes while avoiding double taxation; fosters transparent, cooperative relationships with tax authorities (including Italy’s Cooperative Compliance since 2016); employs a comprehensive monitoring system; Board-approved, periodically reviewed, implemented by the Tax Function.

text:
Code of conduct : 
The code of conduct is available on our website. In line with corporate culture and values (Caring, Ownership, Integrity), the code of conduct entails 
principles which all employees and partnering third parties of UniCredit must comply with, to ensure high standards of profes sional conduct and 
integrity related to their activity in, or on behalf of UniCredit. This code provides general principles of conduct abou t key compliance risk (i.e., client 
interest protection, antitrust, market integrity, anti-money laundering an d counter -terrorist financing, financial sanctions, anti-bribery and anti-
corruption, data protection), which are periodically monitored by respective functions.  
 
The Code of Conduct is approved by the Board of Directors and applies to all UniCredit’s legal entities. The Board of Directo rs of UniCredit, the 
Chief Executive Officer, as well as the rest of the top management of UniCredit and the Group legal entities are responsible for creating a general 
culture of risk management in the organization and ensuring the oversight of the desired conduct. In this regard, they play a n active role to enforce 
the behavioural  standards described in this policy19.

title: Group tax strategy policy:
heading: Group tax strategy policy :
start_phrase: UniCredit Group complies, in form and substance, with all domestic, international or supranational tax laws, regulations and practices, and cooperates with full transparency with the Tax Authorities of all jurisdictions where it operates.
summary:
- Outlines UniCredit’s global policy against harassment, sexual misconduct, bullying, and retaliation, aligned with the Universal Declaration of Human Rights; applies across all Group entities and covers internal/external behavior, prevention, detection, enforcement, support for reporters, protection from retaliation, and promotion of diversity and inclusion.

- Describes the Group privacy policy establishing a Group-wide framework for personal data protection in line with GDPR and local laws; clarifies accountability of Data Controllers and the advisory role of Data Protection Officers; aims to build trust with customers and stakeholders.
- Details Customer Protection rules for offering banking products and services, embedding EU regulatory requirements (Consumer Credit, Mortgage Credit, Payment Accounts, PSD2 transparency, Deposit Guarantee Schemes, and EBA product governance guidelines); applicable to all channels and customer segments, with implementation monitored internally.
- Summarizes the Code of Conduct, grounded in the values Caring, Ownership, Integrity, setting standards for all employees and third parties across key compliance risks (client protection, antitrust, market integrity, AML/CFT and sanctions, anti-bribery/corruption, data protection); approved by the Board, with leadership responsible for promoting desired conduct.

text:
Group tax strategy policy : 
UniCredit Group complies, in form and substance, with all domestic, international or supranational tax laws, regulations and practices, and 
cooperates with full transparency with the Tax Authorities of all jurisdictions where it operates. In particular, th e goal of UniCredit group is to pay all 
taxes due and promptly implement all obligations required by applicable tax laws; and at the same time, maintain the Group's global tax efficiency, 
avoiding double taxation.  
 
The UniCredit group also seeks to establish good and cooperative relationships and dialogue with the Tax Authorities in the various countrie s in 
which it conducts business. UniCredit S .p.A. in fact, has joined the Italian Tax Cooperative Compliance Regime since 2016.  
 
In addition, given the complexity of tax law, to ensure the achievement of such objectives, the UniCredit group has adopted a comprehensive 
monitoring system to verify that its tax obligations are complied with on time and in full.  
 
The tax strategy p olicy is approved by the Board of Directors, and it is brought to the attention of all the companies in the UniCredit group, also 
through its availability on Group intranet and internet website. The policy is subject to periodic review by UniCredit’s internal experts on tax and 
compliance. In particular, the Tax Function is in charge of the tax strategy policy implementation and update.

- Whistleblowing procedure: Protects whistleblowers and prohibits retaliation in line with EU Directive 2019/1937; encourages reporting by employees and third parties via defined channels; covers illegal, unfair, unethical conduct, regulatory breaches, and internal rule violations; approved by the CEO; aligned with the Code of Conduct and anti-harassment policy; published on the website.

text:
Whistleblowing procedure : 
The principal object of the Whistleblowing procedure is to guarantee the protection of the whistleblowers who report misconduct referred or impacted 
on the working environment, and to ensure the absence of retaliation, in line with the European Whistleblowing Directive 1937 /2019.  
 
The purpose of this rule is to promote a corporate environment where employees and third parties are encouraged to report una cceptable conduct 
(through the defined adequate communication channels) within the Group as a valuable contribution to self -correct ion and excellence. Unacceptable 
Conduct refers to any action and/or omission in a work -related context or impacting it, that is or could be harmful to or jeopardise the Group and/or 
its Employees, including conduct that is:  
• illegal, unfair or unethical;  
• a breach of laws and regulations, including but not limited to E uropean Union laws; or  
• a failure to comply with internal rules.  
 
The Group respects , and all the e mployees and the third parties are required to respect , all applicable international, national, and local laws and 
regulations. There may be countries where the Group's standards and requirements may exceed the requirements of that jurisdic tion. Also, this 
policy, approved by the CEO, should be read in conjunc tion with the global policy code of conduct and the global policy against harassment, sexual 
misconduct, b ullying and retaliation, as implemented in each legal entity. The policy is available on our website.

- Anti-fraud policy: Establishes a fraud management system, roles, and responsibilities to identify, assess, and mitigate internal/external fraud risks; covers EU Directive 2015/2366 requirements; Group Security responsible; applicable to UniCredit S.p.A. and addressed to all entities.

text:
Supplier qualification process : 
Aligned with International Labour Organization's (ILO) Fundamental Human Rights Conventions and the UN Global Compact princip les, the supplier 
qualification process defines the criteria and methods of third -party screening prior to the involvement of the supplier in a possible sourcing action for 
the purchase of goods/services as part of the activities managed by Procurement. The qualification of suppliers allows to:  
• identify adequate suppliers based on compliance, sustainability and economic -financial criteria in line with the Group's policies and guidelines;  
• manage risks associated with third parties (e.g. corruption risk, reputational risks, economic risks, etc.) by excluding suppl iers who have not 
succeeded in the qualification process;  
• promote, to suppliers, ethical principles and policies in sustainability;  
• arrange from time to time a list of successful suppliers in the qualification process that can be used for sourcing activities  managed by 
Procurement structures.  
 
The supplier qualification process is performed when the negotiation and purchase of goods/services are carried out centrally  by Group 
Procurement, which is the responsible function: not all Group purchases are handled by Procurement, as there are purchase  categories and/or 
thresholds managed outside of Procurement.  
 
The screening on suppliers is based on risk scores provided by external risk info -providers and on other specific controls acted by Procurement 
and/or Compliance to verify mainly anti -corruption aspects and negative news. When risk scores are unavailable f rom info- providers the supplier 
evaluation is based, by exception, on supplier’s questionnaires, which also take into consideration environmental and social aspects. The supplier 
qualification must be periodically reviewed. In any case, a monitoring functi onality, able to notify risk -related incidents or changing in the risk scores, 
is in place.

title: Expenditure regulation:
heading: Expenditure regulation :
start_phrase: This global policy has the purpose to define principles and minimum requirements necessary to manage expenditures and investm ents, from demand to pay.
summary:
- Scope and governance: A Group-wide policy, approved by the CEO, applies to all UniCredit legal entities, governing bodies, employees, tied agents, and temporary staff, to be implemented in line with local laws, adopting the stricter local requirements where applicable.

- Supplier screening mechanics: Centralized by Group Procurement for centrally managed purchases; uses external risk provider scores, anti‑corruption and adverse news checks by Procurement/Compliance; relies on questionnaires (including environmental/social aspects) when data are unavailable; includes periodic reviews and incident/risk score change monitoring.
- Expenditure regulation: Defines principles/minimum requirements for managing expenditures and investments from demand to payment; distinguishes P&L expenditures from multi‑year investments.

- Mortgages to households: For collateralized loans, assesses “Acquisition” perimeter under Delegated Regulation 2021/2139; excludes “Renovation” and motor vehicles due to data limitations; identifies “green loans” using Energy Performance Certificate and Primary Energy Demand data for eligibility KPIs.

demand to pay.  
 
This policy applies to all disbursements incurred to perform activities in all legal entities of the Group, classified in expenditu res and investments 
according to the following:  
• expenditures are all disbursements linked to the procurement of goods and services that have economic impact on P&L;  
• investments are related to the procurement of goods and services that are long -term and have a multi -year utility.  
 
The functions involved in the process disciplined by such policy are:  
• Group Cost Management, in charge of steering the expenditure approval process at Group level, monitoring the evolution of Gro up and UniCredit

• Group Procurement, in charge of managing centrally the purchases of goods and services for the Group in order to achieve cost  optimization.

title: Introduction
heading: Introduction
start_phrase: The following tables display the disclosure obligations under Article 8 of the Disclosures Delegated Act supplementing the EU Taxonomy Regulation (2020/852), which requires financial companies to report Taxonomy eligibility and alignment’s key performance indicators (KPIs), starting for calendar year 2023.
summary:
- Group-wide governance policy: Approved by the CEO and applicable to all UniCredit Group legal entities, governing bodies, employees, tied agents, and temporary staff across all activities. It must be applied in line with local laws, adopting stricter local requirements where applicable.

- Anti-fraud policy: Establishes a fraud management system to identify, understand, and assess internal and external fraud risks; sets roles and responsibilities for fraud governance; incorporates requirements from EU Directive 2015/2366; Group Security is responsible for implementation.

- Supplier qualification process: Aligned with ILO Fundamental Conventions and UN Global Compact; defines pre-engagement screening of third parties to:
  - Select suppliers based on compliance, sustainability, and financial criteria.
  - Manage third-party risks (corruption, reputational, economic) by excluding non-qualified suppliers.
  - Promote ethical and sustainability principles.
  - Maintain a qualified supplier list for sourcing.
  Screening relies on external risk scores and Procurement/Compliance checks (anti-corruption, adverse news). Where scores are unavailable, supplier questionnaires (including environmental and social aspects) are used. Qualification is periodically reviewed with ongoing risk monitoring. Central purchasing is managed by Group Procurement; some categories/thresholds sit outside Procurement.

- Expenditure regulation: Global policy setting principles and minimum requirements to manage expenditures and investments end-to-end (demand to pay). Applies to all Group disbursements:
  - Expenditures: goods/services impacting P&L.
  - Investments: long-term, multi-year utility goods/services.
  Key functions:
  - Group Cost Management: steers approvals, monitors Group and UniCredit S.p.A. non-HR costs, manages Group ICT demand, and supports the Projects & Expenses Committee (PEC).
  - Group Procurement: central purchasing to optimize costs.

- Environmental information (EU Taxonomy Article 8 disclosure):
  - Scope and intent: Provides KPIs on Taxonomy eligibility and alignment to enhance transparency and support transition to a low-carbon economy; focuses on undertakings under NFRD 2014/95/EU; main metric is the Green Asset Ratio (GAR).
  - Data considerations: Only counterparties with mandatory non-financial disclosures are included; exposures to central governments, central banks, and supranationals are excluded; data gaps from non-reporting counterparties reduce coverage.
  - 2024 results: Turnover-based GAR of 1.36% with total GAR assets of €547bn, up from 1.16% with €551bn at year-end 2023; primarily driven by climate change mitigation-aligned exposures.
  - Methodology:
    - Portfolio segmented by asset type; counterparties’ own KPIs used (no use-of-proceeds treatment); T-1 templates published but not directly comparable due to perimeter changes.
    - Financial and non-financial corporates and financial guarantees: KPIs derived as weighted averages of financing and counterparties’ Taxonomy-aligned activities; NFRD reports sourced via an external provider; where a subsidiary contributes to a parent’s KPI, parent KPIs are mapped to the counterparty; if no split between climate mitigation (CCM) and adaptation (CCA), values reported under TOTAL columns, which may exceed the sum of components.
    - Loans collateralized to households: Focus on “Acquisition” perimeter per Delegated Regulation 2021/2139 (excluding “Renovation” and “Motor vehicles” due to data gaps); “green loans” identified using EPC and Primary Energy Demand criteria for top-performing buildings for Eligibility KPIs.
text:
Introduction  
The following tables display the disclosure obligations under Article 8 of the Disclosures Delegated Act supplementing the EU  Taxonomy Regulation 
(2020/852), which requires financial companies to report Taxonomy eligibility and alignment’s key performance indicators (KPIs), starting for 
calendar year 2023. The disclosure is intended to provide transparency on sustainability and facilitate the transition toward s a low -carbon economy. 
In particular, the Article 8 of the Regulation requires undertakings covere d by the Non -Financial Reporting Directive (NFRD) 2014/95/EU to publish 
information on how and to what extent their economic activities qualify as environmentally sustainable under the Taxonomy Reg ulation. The result is 
presented through the green asset ra tio (GAR), that is the exposures to activities that are Taxonomy aligned (numerator) divided by total covered 
assets (denominator).  
 
As of today, for the GAR calculation , actual data disclosed by counterparties are necessary to assess banks’ Taxonomy -related KPIs for financial 
and non -financial undertakings. This means that undertakings that are not covered by mandatory non -financial disclosure are excluded, and the data 
gap is reflected on the bank’s ratio.  
 
This year, the GAR Turnover -based is 1.36% with total GAR assets equal to €547 billion , compared to year -end 2023 where the GAR was 1.16% 
with total GAR assets equal to €551 billion. The GAR  is mainly explained by exposures contributing to the climate change mitigation objective.

title: Our calculation approach
heading: Our calculation approach
start_phrase: In accordance with the templates provided by Regulation, for the calculation of the GAR KPIs, we have differentiated the portf olio by assets and applied different calculation approaches, where required.
summary:
- Group-wide policy governance: CEO-approved policy applies to all UniCredit Group entities, governing bodies, employees, tied agents and temps, and across all business activities; stricter local laws prevail over Group principles.
- Anti-fraud policy: establishes a Group fraud management system to identify, assess and manage internal/external fraud risks, protect assets, and define roles/responsibilities; aligned with EU Directive 2015/2366; Group Security is responsible for implementation and it applies to UniCredit S.p.A. and all Group entities.
- Supplier qualification process: aligned with ILO Fundamental Conventions and UN Global Compact; sets third-party screening criteria to select compliant, sustainable, and financially sound suppliers; manages third-party risks (corruption, reputational, economic), promotes ethical/sustainability principles, and maintains a qualified supplier list. Screening uses external risk scores plus Procurement/Compliance checks (anti-corruption, adverse news); if scores unavailable, uses questionnaires including environmental/social aspects; periodic reviews and incident/risk-score monitoring in place. Applies to centrally managed purchases by Group Procurement; some categories/thresholds lie outside Procurement.
- Expenditure regulation: global policy defining principles and minimum requirements from demand to pay; applies to all Group disbursements. Distinguishes expenditures (P&L impact) from investments (long-term, multi-year utility). Roles: Group Cost Management (steers approvals, monitors Group and UniCredit S.p.A. NHR costs, manages ICT demand, supports Projects & Expenses Committee), and Group Procurement (centralizes purchasing for cost optimization).
- Environmental information (EU Taxonomy Article 8):
  - Purpose and scope: discloses Taxonomy eligibility/alignment KPIs under the Disclosures Delegated Act for entities under NFRD; transparency to support low-carbon transition. Key metric is Green Asset Ratio (GAR): Taxonomy-aligned exposures over total covered assets.
  - Data constraints: relies on counterparties’ mandatory non-financial disclosures; non-reporting undertakings are excluded, affecting ratios.
  - Results: 2024 GAR Turnover-based is 1.36% with total GAR assets of €547bn, up from 1.16% and €551bn in 2023; mainly driven by climate change mitigation exposures.
  - Methodology: portfolio segmented per regulatory templates; includes only NFRD-reporting undertakings; excludes central governments, central banks, and supranationals; uses counterparty KPIs only (no use-of-proceeds within Article 8 templates). T-1 templates published but not comparable due to a changed 2024 perimeter.
  - Segment approaches:
    - Financial and Non-Financial Corporations, and Financial Guarantees: KPIs based on weighted average financing and counterparties’ share of Taxonomy-aligned activities; NFRD data collected via an external provider; includes entities that directly/indirectly meet NFRD scope; where subsidiaries contribute to parent KPIs, parent KPIs applied; if no CCM/CCA breakdown, totals are reported across all six environmental objectives, so totals may exceed the sum of individual components.
    - Loans collateralized to households: focuses on the “Acquisition” perimeter (DR 2021/2139); excludes “Renovation” and motor vehicles due to data gaps; identifies green loans via Energy Performance Certificate and Primary Energy Demand criteria for eligibility.
text:
Our calculation approach  
In accordance with the templates provided by Regulation, for the calculation of the GAR KPIs, we have differentiated the portf olio by assets and 
applied different calculation approaches, where required. We have only included undertakings subject to NFRD wit h mandatory disclosures, 
excluding exposures to central governments, central banks, and supranational issuers.  Information related to the use of proceeds is not published 
within the framework of the Article 8 Taxonomy templates. Therefore, the sole counte rparty KPIs are taken into account to define eligibility and 
alignment.  Furthermore, as required by the Regulation, the T -1 templates have been published but it should be noted that the comparison is not 
significant as the perimeter of the 2024 disclosure has been changed compared to that of last year. In details, below a description of the applied 
approach.  
 
• Financial Corporations, Non- Financial Corporations, and Financial Guarantees : the Taxonomy KPIs consist of the weighted average of 
financing activities and the proportion of Taxonomy -aligned economic activities of the counterparty. The collection of reports disclosed by our 
counterparties, according to the NFRD, was done with the support of an external provide r. 
- When identifying NFRD counterparties, we have included all corporations which by themselves or indirectly fulfil criteria of the mandatory NFRD 
requirements. Moreover, when a counterparty has contributed to the parent’s reported KPIs, we have included the value for the counterparty by 
using the KPIs of the parent company.  
- We encountered cases where a counterparty, in its NFRD disclosure, did not report the breakdown of its Taxonomy KPIs among CC M and CCA.

Disclosure pursuant to Article 8 of Regulation 2020/852 (EU Taxonomy Regulation)  
 
Introduction  
The following tables display the disclosure obligations under Article 8 of the Disclosures Delegated Act supplementing the EU  Taxonomy Regulation 
(2020/852), which requires financial companies to report Taxonomy eligibility and alignment’s key performance indicators (KPIs), starting for 
calendar year 2023. The disclosure is intended to provide transparency on sustainability and facilitate the transition toward s a low -carbon economy. 
In particular, the Article 8 of the Regulation requires undertakings covere d by the Non -Financial Reporting Directive (NFRD) 2014/95/EU to publish 
information on how and to what extent their economic activities qualify as environmentally sustainable under the Taxonomy Reg ulation. The result is 
presented through the green asset ra tio (GAR), that is the exposures to activities that are Taxonomy aligned (numerator) divided by total covered 
assets (denominator).  
 
As of today, for the GAR calculation , actual data disclosed by counterparties are necessary to assess banks’ Taxonomy -related KPIs for financial 
and non -financial undertakings. This means that undertakings that are not covered by mandatory non -financial disclosure are excluded, and the data 
gap is reflected on the bank’s ratio.  
 
This year, the GAR Turnover -based is 1.36% with total GAR assets equal to €547 billion , compared to year -end 2023 where the GAR was 1.16% 
with total GAR assets equal to €551 billion. The GAR  is mainly explained by exposures contributing to the climate change mitigation objective.

- Group-wide policy governance: CEO-approved policy applicable to all UniCredit Group legal entities, governing bodies, employees, tied agents and temps, across all activities; compliance with local laws with stricter local requirements prevailing.
- Anti-fraud policy: aims to identify, assess and manage internal/external fraud risks; defines Group-wide fraud management system, roles and responsibilities; incorporates EU Directive (EU) 2015/2366 requirements; Group Security responsible for implementation.
- Supplier qualification process: aligned with ILO Core Conventions and UN Global Compact; sets screening criteria and methods to assess suppliers on compliance, sustainability and financial soundness; manages third-party risks (corruption, reputational, economic) by excluding non-qualified suppliers; promotes ethical and sustainability principles; maintains qualified supplier lists for sourcing; primarily managed centrally by Group Procurement (not all purchases fall under Procurement); risk screening via external providers plus Procurement/Compliance checks on anti-corruption and adverse news; questionnaires used by exception; periodic reviews and ongoing risk monitoring.
- Expenditure regulation: global policy defining principles and minimum requirements to manage expenditures and investments from demand to payment; applies to all disbursements across the Group; distinguishes expenditures (P&L impact) vs investments (multi-year utility); roles include Group Cost Management (steering approvals, monitoring Group and UniCredit S.p.A. NHR costs, managing ICT demand, PEC activities) and Group Procurement (centralized purchasing for cost optimization).
- EU Taxonomy Article 8 environmental disclosures:
  - GAR (green asset ratio) Turnover-based is 1.36% on €547bn total GAR assets in 2024 (vs 1.16% on €551bn in 2023), mainly driven by climate change mitigation activities.
  - Methodological scope: includes only undertakings under NFRD mandatory reporting; excludes central governments, central banks and supranationals; uses counterparties’ actual reported KPIs; use-of-proceeds data not included, so only counterparty KPIs considered; T-1 templates published but not comparable due to scope changes.
  - Financial and non-financial corporates and financial guarantees: KPIs based on weighted average of financing activities and counterparties’ Taxonomy-aligned activity share; data gathered via external provider; NFRD scope includes direct and indirect (via parent) reporters, using parent KPIs where applicable; when CCM/CCA split is missing, values reported in TOTAL column.
  - Loans collateralized to households: focuses on “Acquisition” perimeter (excludes “Renovation” and “Motor vehicles” green-loan identification constraints); eligibility uses EPC and PED; alignment for assets built before 31 Dec 2020 with documented EPC=A; Italy only Top-15% approach for pre-2020; NZEB approach for assets built after 31 Dec 2020; conservative DNSH physical risk assessment aligned with Pillar 3 Template 5, no adaptation plans considered.
  - Motor vehicles to households: eligible if loans finance vehicle purchases; aligned only if financing low-emission vehicles.
  - Assets under Management: perimeter based on Group external reporting of collective investment funds; numerator is weighted average of portfolio-level Taxonomy-aligned proportions using underlying holdings’ actual KPIs via external provider; total AuM includes all asset classes, while “of which” figures include only equity and debt (so totals can exceed components).
  - New business flow: calculated as transaction-level delta stock between year-end 2024 and year-end 2023 to capture new originations.
  - Nuclear and gas-related activities: eligibility, non-eligibility and alignment disclosed per amended Disclosures Delegated Act (Art. 8(6)-(8)); computed using latest available KPIs for NFRD-subject non-financial counterparties.

summary:
- Outlines UniCredit’s methodology for EU Taxonomy eligibility and alignment KPIs within the Sustainability Statement, applying conservative assumptions and external data sources.
- Real estate exposures: considers only documented EPC=A for assets built before Dec 31, 2020; applies a Top-15% energy performance approach for Italian counterparties (pre-2020) and the NZEB (Nearly Zero Energy Building) approach for assets built after Dec 31, 2020; NZEB and Top-15% data collected by region via an external provider.
- Do No Significant Harm (DNSH) assessment integrates physical climate risk analysis aligned with Pillar 3 Template 5 thresholds and climate data; excludes adaptation plans and other mitigating actions.
- Motor vehicles to households: eligibility covers loans for vehicle purchases; alignment limited to loans for low-emission vehicles.

- New business flow: measured as transaction-level delta stock between Dec 31, 2024 and Dec 31, 2023 to capture new originations.
- Additional disclosures on nuclear energy and fossil gas per Article 8(6)-(8) of the amended Disclosures Delegated Act (effective Jan 1, 2023); KPIs computed using the most recent data for non-financial corporate counterparties subject to the NFRD.

heading: • Asset Under Management (AuM) :
start_phrase: the reporting perimeter of the AuM KPIs is based on the volumes of collective investment funds which the Group reports in the Group Full Year Results Market Presentation and other external communications .
summary:
- Explains UniCredit’s methodology for EU Taxonomy eligibility and alignment KPIs within the sustainability statement, using conservative assumptions and external data sources.
- Buildings: counts only documented EPC A for assets built before Dec 31, 2020; applies Top-15% approach for Italian assets pre-2021 and NZEB (Nearly Zero Energy Building) criteria for assets built after Dec 31, 2020; NZEB and Top-15% data sourced externally.
- DNSH assessment: integrates physical climate risk analysis aligned with Pillar 3 Template 5 thresholds and data; excludes adaptation plans or other mitigants.
- Motor vehicles to households: eligibility covers loans for vehicle purchases; alignment restricted to loans financing low-emission vehicles.
- Assets Under Management (AuM) KPIs: perimeter based on collective investment funds disclosed in Group external communications; numerator is a weighted average share of Taxonomy-aligned activities at portfolio level; KPIs derived from underlying holdings’ market-available data via an external provider; total AuM includes all asset classes, while “of which” categories cover only debt and equity, so totals may exceed the sum of components.
- New Business metric: calculated as transaction-level delta stock between Dec 31, 2024 and Dec 31, 2023, capturing only newly originated transactions.
- Nuclear and fossil gas disclosures: reports eligibility, non-eligibility, and alignment per Article 8(6)-(8) of the amended Disclosures Delegated Act (effective Jan 1, 2023); KPIs based on latest data from non-financial corporate counterparties subject to NFRD.

the reporting perimeter of the AuM KPIs is based on the volumes of collective investment funds which the 
Group reports in the Group Full Year Results Market Presentation  and other external communications . The numerator is calculated as a weighted

portfolio aggregated KPIs, which are the results of calculations p erformed on underlying holdings’ actual KPIs available to  the market, was

- The total value of AuM includes all types of asset class funds, while the ‘of which’ only includes debt and equity respective ly as classified by our

title: Additional disclosure on Nuclear and Gas related activities
heading: • Additional disclosure on Nuclear and Gas related activities :
start_phrase: we have disclosed the eligibility, non -eligibility, and alignment of nuclear energy and fossil gas related activities in accordance with Article 8(6), (7) and (8) of the amended Disclosures Delegated Act as of 1 January 2023.
summary:
- Purpose and scope: Extract from UniCredit’s 2024 Annual Reports and Accounts, Sustainability statements, providing EU Taxonomy Article 8 disclosures for credit institutions, including methodologies and detailed quantitative KPIs (GAR stock and flow, off-balance sheet KPIs), with Annex VI templates.

- Methodology highlights:
  - Real estate alignment: For assets built before Dec 31, 2020, only documented EPC=A counted; for Italy, Top-15% energy performance approach applied; for assets built after Dec 31, 2020, NZEB (Nearly Zero Energy Building) approach used. Regional NZEB and Top-15% data sourced from an external provider. Conservative stance (only adequate documentation considered).
  - DNSH assessment: Integrates analysis of physical climate risks aligned with thresholds and climate data used in Pillar 3 Template 5; excludes adaptation plans or other mitigating actions for conservatism.
  - Household vehicles: Eligible exposures are loans for motor vehicle purchases; aligned exposures limited to low-emission vehicles.
  - Assets under Management (AuM): Perimeter based on collective investment funds disclosed in Group external communications. Alignment calculated via weighted average of portfolio-level Taxonomy-aligned proportions using external provider data on underlying holdings’ KPIs. Total AuM includes all asset classes; “of which debt/equity” only includes those classes, so totals can exceed the sum of components.
  - New business (flow): Determined via transaction-level delta stock between Dec 31, 2024 and Dec 31, 2023 (new originations only).
  - Nuclear and gas: Eligibility, non-eligibility, and alignment disclosed per Article 8(6)-(8) of the amended Disclosures Delegated Act (effective Jan 1, 2023); KPIs calculated for NFRD-subject non-financial counterparties using most recent data.

- Summary KPIs (as presented):
  - Green Asset Ratio (GAR) stock: Total environmentally sustainable assets €7,432m; 1.36% turnover-based and 1.91% CapEx-based; coverage over total assets 68.99%; 56.10% of assets excluded from the numerator; 31.01% excluded from the denominator.
  - GAR flow: €2,208m; 2.19% turnover-based and 3.42% CapEx-based; coverage 26.94%.
  - Additional KPIs: Financial guarantees €291m (5.81% turnover-based; 10.73% CapEx-based). AuM €3,225m (9.22% turnover-based; 14.12% CapEx-based).

- Detailed GAR composition (turnover- and CapEx-based):
  - Comprehensive breakdowns by counterparty type (financial undertakings, non-financial undertakings, households, local governments), instrument (loans, debt securities including UoP, equity), and environmental objectives (CCM, CCA, WTR, CE, PPC, BIO), including use-of-proceeds, transitional, and enabling categories.
  - Households: Large eligible exposure primarily through residential mortgages; aligned portions include eligible building loans and low-emission vehicle loans.
  - Exclusions and coverage: Significant portions excluded from GAR numerator or denominator per Article 7 (e.g., SMEs and NFCs not subject to NFRD, non-EU non-NFRD counterparties). Assets not covered for GAR include central governments/supranationals, central bank exposures, and trading book items.

- Comparative view 2024 vs 2023:
  - Increase in Taxonomy-aligned amounts and ratios year over year (e.g., total aligned under turnover approach rising from €6,396m in 2023 to €7,432m in 2024; higher CapEx-based alignment).
  - Expanded off-balance sheet disclosures with higher eligible/aligned figures for financial guarantees and AuM.

- Data sourcing and conservatism: Reliance on external providers for building performance benchmarks and AuM portfolio KPIs; strict documentation requirements and exclusion of mitigation/adaptation plans emphasize conservative alignment measurement.

summary:
- Part of UniCredit’s 2024 Annual Reports and Accounts (Consolidated report on operations – Sustainability statements) focusing on EU Taxonomy disclosures and the Green Asset Ratio (GAR).
- Detailed CapEx-based GAR tables as of 31.12.2024 with 31.12.2023 comparatives:
  - Breakdown of total assets into GAR-covered assets and assets not covered for GAR (e.g., central governments/supranationals, central banks, trading book).
  - Segmentation by counterparty and product: financial undertakings (credit institutions, other financial corporations, insurance), non-financial undertakings, households, SMEs/NFCs not subject to NFRD, non‑EU counterparties; loans and advances (including residential/commercial real estate, building renovation, motor vehicles), debt securities (including use-of-proceeds), equity instruments, derivatives, interbank, cash, and other assets.
  - Identification of assets excluded from the GAR numerator but included in the denominator.
  - Taxonomy mapping across the six environmental objectives: climate change mitigation (CCM), climate change adaptation (CCA), water and marine resources (WTR), circular economy (CE), pollution prevention and control (PPC), biodiversity and ecosystems (BIO).
  - Clear split between taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned exposures, with “of which” breakdowns for use-of-proceeds instruments, transitional and enabling activities.
  - Totals presented, including 2024 total assets and total GAR assets, and the objective-by-objective eligible/aligned amounts.
- Off-balance sheet disclosures for undertakings subject to NFRD:
  - Financial guarantees and assets under management (with sub-breakdowns into debt and equity securities), showing taxonomy-eligible and aligned components and “of which” use-of-proceeds/enabling/transitional splits.
- Collateral obtained by taking possession (residential and commercial property) shown with taxonomy eligibility/alignment detail.
- Year-on-year comparison (2024 vs 2023) highlighting movements in GAR-covered assets, eligible/aligned amounts, and off-balance sheet taxonomy metrics.
- GAR sector information (Turnover-based) for 31.12.2024:
  - NACE 4-digit breakdown for non-financial corporates subject to NFRD, listing specific subsectors (e.g., chemicals and rubber/plastics manufacturing).
  - Gross carrying amounts per environmental objective and identification of the environmentally sustainable portions at sector level.

summary:
- Focus: EU Taxonomy Green Asset Ratio (GAR) disclosures within UniCredit’s Sustainability Statement of the 2024 Annual Reports and Accounts, as at 31.12.2024.
- Content type: Detailed, turnover-based sector breakdown (in € million) and related KPI percentages for assets in scope of GAR, following EU Taxonomy/NFRD/EBA templates.

What the tables cover
- GAR sector information – Turnover based:
  - Granular breakdown by NACE Rev. 2 four‑digit sectors for non‑financial corporates subject to NFRD.
  - For each sector: gross carrying amount and “of which environmentally sustainable” amounts mapped to the six EU Taxonomy environmental objectives:
    - Climate Change Mitigation (CCM)
    - Climate Change Adaptation (CCA)
    - Sustainable use and protection of Water and Marine Resources (WTR)
    - Transition to a Circular Economy (CE)
    - Pollution prevention and control (PPC)
    - Protection and restoration of Biodiversity and Ecosystems (BIO)
  - A total column consolidates environmentally sustainable amounts across all objectives.
  - Coverage spans manufacturing (chemicals, cement, metals, electronics, machinery, vehicles), utilities (electricity production/transmission/distribution, gas, steam), water and waste (water supply, waste collection/treatment, recovery), construction and civil engineering (buildings, roads, rail, utilities, water projects), transport (rail, road services, water), telecommunications and IT, real estate (buy/sell, rental and operating, management), professional and research services, leasing, and selected social care activities.
  - Illustrative sectors with notable environmentally sustainable amounts include:
    - Electricity: production, transmission and distribution (D35.x), showing significant CCM alignment and some contributions to other objectives.
    - Water and waste: water collection/treatment/supply (E36.00) spanning CCM, CCA, WTR; waste collection and treatment (E38.11/E38.21) with strong Circular Economy components.
    - Transport and infrastructure: rail construction and services (F42.12; H49.10/H49.20) and utility projects for electricity/telecom (F42.22) showing CCM alignment.
    - Manufacturing: basic iron and steel (C24.10), cement (C23.51), selected electrical/electronic equipment (C26–C27), machinery for paper production (C28.95), and motor vehicles (C29.10) with CCM and some CCA entries.
    - Real estate: rental/operating of own or leased real estate (L68.20) with material CCM/CCA totals.
    - Leasing of cars and light vehicles (N77.11) contributing to CCM.

- GAR KPI (stock) – Turnover based – Percentages:
  - Presents the proportion of total covered assets funding Taxonomy‑relevant (eligible) and Taxonomy‑aligned activities for CCM, CCA and WTR, including “of which” categories (use of proceeds, transitional, enabling, as applicable).
  - Breakdown by counterparty segments:
    - Financial undertakings (credit institutions, other financials, management companies, insurance undertakings)
    - Non‑financial undertakings
    - Households (including loans collateralised by residential property, building renovation loans, motor vehicle loans)
    - Local governments (housing and other)
    - Collateral obtained (residential and commercial real estate)
  - Headline indications:
    - Total GAR assets represent about 20.2% of total covered assets, with c.1.32% Taxonomy‑aligned for CCM, including identified use‑of‑proceeds, transitional and enabling portions.
    - Small but positive shares are reported for CCA and WTR eligibility/alignment.
    - Households show a sizable eligible share driven by mortgage exposure, with a measurable aligned component via use‑of‑proceeds.
    - Non‑financial corporates contribute to both eligible and aligned CCM shares; financial undertakings add smaller aligned portions mainly via securities and equity holdings.

Purpose and use
- Demonstrates UniCredit’s exposure to Taxonomy‑eligible and aligned activities at detailed sector level, quantifying environmentally sustainable financing by objective and aggregating to KPI percentages, in line with EU GAR disclosure requirements.

title: GAR KPI (stock) - Turnover based - % (compared to total covered assets in the denominator)
heading: 3 GAR KPI (stock) - Turnover based - % (compared to total covered assets in the denominator)
summary:
- The extract presents UniCredit’s EU Taxonomy Green Asset Ratio (GAR) stock disclosures within the Sustainability Statement of the 2024 Annual Reports and Accounts, detailing the share of total covered assets that fund taxonomy-relevant sectors, split between taxonomy-eligible and taxonomy-aligned activities.
- It provides turnover-based GAR KPIs as of 31.12.2024 and 31.12.2023 across the six environmental objectives (climate change mitigation, climate change adaptation, water and marine resources, circular economy, pollution prevention and control, biodiversity and ecosystems), with breakdowns by:
  - Counterparty/segment: financial undertakings (credit institutions, other financial corporations, management companies, insurance), non-financial undertakings, households, and local governments.
  - Asset class: loans and advances, debt securities (including use-of-proceeds instruments), equity instruments, and collateralized immovable properties.
  - Instrument type flags: of which use of proceeds, transitional, and enabling activities.
- 2024 turnover-based results highlight:
  - Total taxonomy-eligible assets: 20.46% of total covered assets; taxonomy-aligned: 1.36%.
  - Coverage of total assets in the GAR perimeter: 68.99%.
  - Key contributors: households (eligible 17.28%, aligned 0.51%, largely residential mortgages), non-financial undertakings (eligible 1.56%, aligned 0.63%), and financial undertakings (eligible 1.60%, aligned 0.21%). Use-of-proceeds, transitional, and enabling shares are generally small.
- Year-on-year comparison (2023 vs 2024, turnover-based):
  - Eligible increased from 19.20% to 20.46%; aligned rose from 1.16% to 1.36%.
  - GAR coverage remained broadly stable (~69%).
  - Notable movements include a sharp rise in identified household building renovation loans (eligible from 0.04% to 0.40%) and improved alignment for non-financial undertakings, while household aligned share declined modestly (0.60% to 0.51%).
- The extract also includes 2024 capex-based GAR KPIs (for CCM, CCA, WTR):
  - Total taxonomy-eligible: 20.67%; taxonomy-aligned: 1.84%.
  - Breakdown mirrors the turnover view: financial undertakings (eligible 1.56%, aligned 0.30%), non-financial undertakings (eligible 1.81%, aligned 1.02%), and households (aligned 0.51% via residential mortgages).

heading: 3 GAR KPI (stock) - Capex based - % (compared to total covered assets in the denominator)
summary:
- Section context: Extract from UniCredit’s 2024 Annual Reports and Accounts, Consolidated report on operations – Sustainability statement, presenting EU Taxonomy reporting.
- Focus of content: Detailed disclosure of Green Asset Ratio (GAR) KPIs:
  - Stock (Capex-based) metrics as a percentage of total covered assets for 31.12.2024 and 31.12.2023.
  - Flow (Turnover-based) metrics for 2024 as a percentage of the flow of total eligible assets.
- Scope and structure:
  - Breakdowns by EU Taxonomy environmental objectives: Climate Change Mitigation (CCM), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Water and Marine Resources (WTR), Circular Economy (CE), Pollution (PPC), and Biodiversity & Ecosystems (BIO).
  - Classification into Taxonomy-eligible versus Taxonomy-aligned exposures, with “of which” sub-categories for use-of-proceeds, transitional, and enabling activities.
  - Portfolio segmentation: financial undertakings (credit institutions, other financial corporations, management companies, insurance undertakings), non-financial undertakings, households (residential mortgages, building renovation loans, motor vehicle loans), local government financing, and collateral real estate taken into possession.
- 2024 stock highlights (Capex-based):
  - Total Taxonomy-eligible exposures around 21% of total covered assets; Taxonomy-aligned around 1.9%.
  - Approximately 69% of total assets are covered by the GAR denominator.
  - Households, especially residential mortgages, represent the largest share of eligible exposures (~17% of total covered assets), with a notable eligible share in building renovation loans.
  - Non-financial corporates contribute a smaller but material portion of eligible and aligned exposures; financial undertakings show modest aligned shares.
- 2023 stock comparison:
  - Total eligible around 19.7% and aligned around 1.78%, with coverage of total assets also circa 69%, indicating a year-on-year increase in eligible and a slight increase in aligned exposures.
  - Similar portfolio and objective breakdowns provided for comparability.
- 2024 flow highlights (Turnover-based):
  - New origination/movements show CCM as the main driver (c.13% eligible; c.2.1% aligned).
  - Additional aligned contributions from CCA and WTR are present but smaller.
  - By segment, financial undertakings and non-financial corporates contribute to both eligible and aligned flows; households add notably to eligible flows primarily via mortgages.
- Overall purpose: To evidence UniCredit’s alignment with the EU Taxonomy, quantify the share of assets financing environmentally sustainable activities, track progress year-on-year, and distinguish between eligible and fully aligned financing across objectives and portfolio segments.

summary:
- Presents UniCredit’s EU Taxonomy disclosures as part of the Sustainability Statement for year-end 2024, focusing on:
  - Green Asset Ratio (GAR) KPIs for on-balance-sheet assets (flow, Capex-based), and
  - Off-balance-sheet KPIs (stock) for Financial Guarantees and Assets under Management (turnover-based and Capex-based).
- Provides percentages relative to total eligible assets, showing taxonomy-eligible vs taxonomy-aligned shares across all six environmental objectives:
  - Climate Change Mitigation (CCM)
  - Climate Change Adaptation (CCA)
  - Water and Marine Resources (WTR)
  - Circular Economy (CE)
  - Pollution Prevention and Control (PPC)
  - Biodiversity and Ecosystems (BIO)
- Identifies “of which” breakdowns within aligned exposures:
  - Use of Proceeds instruments
  - Transitional activities
  - Enabling activities
- Breaks down exposures by counterparty and instrument type, including:
  - Financial undertakings (credit institutions, other financial corporations, management companies, insurance undertakings)
  - Non-financial undertakings
  - Households (with detail on residential mortgages, building renovation loans, motor vehicle loans)
  - Local government financing and collateral obtained
  - Instruments: loans and advances, debt securities (including Use of Proceeds), equity instruments
- Shows totals for GAR assets and for each off-balance-sheet KPI, enabling comparison of eligible vs aligned portions by environmental objective and by asset/counterparty class.
- Highlights that off-balance-sheet AuM and Financial Guarantees are also mapped to taxonomy objectives, with totals reported for both turnover- and Capex-based views.
- Overall purpose: quantify and transparently disclose the share of new covered assets and off-balance-sheet exposures that are EU Taxonomy-eligible and aligned in 2024, including the nature of alignment (use-of-proceeds, transitional, enabling).

- Extract from UniCredit’s 2024 Annual Reports and Accounts (Consolidated report on operations – Sustainability statements) providing additional disclosure on nuclear and fossil gas activities within the EU Taxonomy/Green Asset Ratio context.
- Confirms the bank carries out, funds, or has exposures to:
  - Nuclear energy activities: R&D/innovation (4.26), construction and safe operation of new installations (4.27), and safe operation of existing installations (4.28) – all marked YES.
  - Fossil gas activities: electricity generation (4.29), combined heat/cool and power (CHP) generation (4.30), and heat generation (4.31) – all marked YES.
- Presents turnover-based EU Taxonomy-aligned economic activities (denominator of applicable KPIs):
  - Specific nuclear/gas rows: minimal aligned amounts recorded only for 4.28 (€7,338k, CCM) and 4.30 (€298k, CCM), both rounding to 0.00% of the KPI; other specified rows show no amounts.
  - “Other” taxonomy-aligned activities (not in 4.26–4.31): €7,290,747k total, representing 1.33% (CCM €7,230,180k; CCA €60,567k).
  - Total applicable KPI: €7,298,383k equating to 1.34% overall (1.33% CCM; 0.01% CCA).
- Overall message: UniCredit discloses the existence of exposures to nuclear and fossil gas-related activities, while the turnover-based taxonomy-aligned amounts for those specific activities are negligible; the vast majority of taxonomy alignment comes from other activities.

- Overall insights: taxonomy-aligned denominators are a small share of totals; alignment is predominantly mitigation-related, with minimal adaptation amounts.

heading: 2 Taxonomy -aligned economic activities (denominator) - CapEx based
summary:
- Extract from UniCredit’s 2024 Annual Reports and Accounts (Consolidated report on operations – Sustainability statements) presenting EU Taxonomy disclosures under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139.
- Focus: amounts and proportions of taxonomy-aligned economic activities for climate objectives—Climate Change Mitigation (CCM) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA)—shown for:
  - Denominator of the applicable KPI (turnover-based)
  - Denominator of the applicable KPI (CapEx-based)
  - Numerator of the applicable KPI (turnover-based)
- Breakdown provided by Annex I/II Sections 4.26–4.31 and an “other taxonomy-aligned economic activities” category.
- Turnover-based denominator:
  - Total applicable KPI: €7,298,383k (1.34%); CCM €7,237,816k (1.33%); CCA €60,567k (0.01%)
  - Notable section amounts: Sec. 4.28 €7,338k; Sec. 4.30 €298k; others largely zero
  - Majority sits in “other taxonomy-aligned” (€7,290,747k; 1.33%)
- CapEx-based denominator:
  - Total applicable KPI: €10,230,348k (1.88%); CCM €10,061,696k (1.84%); CCA €168,652k (0.03%)
  - Notable section amounts: Sec. 4.27 €1,481k; Sec. 4.28 €7,501k; Sec. 4.30 €8,738k; others largely zero
  - Majority in “other taxonomy-aligned” (€10,212,628k; 1.87%)
- Turnover-based numerator:
  - Total taxonomy-aligned turnover: €7,298,383k (100% of aligned turnover); CCM €7,237,816k (99.17%); CCA €60,567k (0.83%)
  - Notable section amounts: Sec. 4.27 €1k; Sec. 4.28 €23,470k; Sec. 4.30 €298k; bulk in “other taxonomy-aligned” (€7,274,614k; 99.67%)
- Main takeaways:
  - Taxonomy alignment is overwhelmingly associated with CCM; CCA represents a small share.
  - Most aligned activity is reported under “other taxonomy-aligned economic activities,” with minimal amounts attributed to specific Sections 4.26–4.31.
  - Several sections show no aligned amounts, indicating concentration of alignment in a limited subset of activities.

heading: 3 Taxonomy -aligned economic activities (numerator) - CapEx based
summary:
- Section of UniCredit’s 2024 Annual Reports and Accounts (Consolidated report on operations – Sustainability statements) presenting EU Taxonomy disclosures under Delegated Regulation 2021/2139.
- Focus: amounts and proportions of EU Taxonomy-aligned economic activities used in KPI numerators (turnover-based and CapEx-based), split between Climate Change Mitigation (CCM) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), and taxonomy-eligible but not aligned activities in the KPI denominator (turnover-based).
- Taxonomy-aligned (turnover-based, numerator):
  - Total: €7,298,383k (100.00%); CCM: €7,237,816k (99.17%); CCA: €60,567k (0.83%).
  - Vast majority classified as “other taxonomy-aligned activities” (row 7); minimal amounts in Annex sections 4.27, 4.28, 4.30; none in 4.26, 4.29, 4.31.
- Taxonomy-aligned (CapEx-based, numerator):
  - Total: €10,230,348k (100.00%); CCM: €10,061,696k (98.35%); CCA: €168,652k (1.65%).
  - Again dominated by “other taxonomy-aligned activities” (row 7); small allocations to sections 4.27, 4.28, 4.29, 4.30; none in 4.26, 4.31.
- Taxonomy-eligible but not aligned (turnover-based, denominator):
  - Total: €103,459,542k (18.97% of the applicable KPI denominator); CCM: €103,355,206k (18.95%); CCA: €104,336k (0.02%).
  - Primarily in “other taxonomy-eligible but not aligned activities” (row 7); small amounts in sections 4.28–4.31; none in 4.26, 4.27.
- Overall takeaway: UniCredit’s taxonomy-aligned exposure is predominantly in climate change mitigation and concentrated in “other” aligned categories, with a smaller share for adaptation; a notable portion of turnover is taxonomy-eligible but not yet aligned.

title: Taxonomy-eligible but not taxonomy-aligned economic activities - Turnover based
heading: 4 Taxonomy -eligible but not taxonomy -aligned economic activities - Turnover based
summary:
- Section context: Sustainability Statement within UniCredit’s 2024 Annual Reports and Accounts (Consolidated report on operations).
- Purpose: EU Taxonomy disclosure of taxonomy-eligible but not taxonomy-aligned economic activities included in the denominator of applicable KPIs, split by climate objectives: Climate Change Mitigation (CCM) and Climate Change Adaptation (CCA).
- Regulatory reference: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139, Annexes I and II, Sections 4.26–4.31, plus an “other taxonomy-eligible” category.
- Turnover-based KPI:
  - Total taxonomy-eligible but not aligned: €103,459,542k (18.97% of denominator).
  - CCM: €103,355,206k (18.95%); CCA: €104,336k (0.02%).
  - Breakdown highlights: zero amounts for Sections 4.26–4.27; small amounts for 4.28 (€548k), 4.29 (€20,897k), 4.30 (€464,977k), 4.31 (€3,046k).
  - “Other taxonomy-eligible not aligned”: €102,970,074k (18.81% total; €102,865,738k CCM; €104,336k CCA).
- CapEx-based KPI:
  - Total taxonomy-eligible but not aligned: €103,465,539k (18.97% of denominator).
  - CCM: €103,129,476k (18.91%); CCA: €336,063k (0.06%).
  - Breakdown highlights: zero amounts for Sections 4.26–4.27; amounts for 4.28 (€1,385k), 4.29 (€11,063k, of which €111k CCA), 4.30 (€310,508k), 4.31 (€8,351k).
  - “Other taxonomy-eligible not aligned”: €103,134,232k (18.84% total; €102,798,280k CCM; €335,952k CCA).
- Key takeaway: Around 19% of the KPI denominators are taxonomy-eligible but not aligned, overwhelmingly linked to CCM, with a very small share to CCA; most amounts sit in the “other taxonomy-eligible” category rather than the specific sections 4.26–4.31.
